# EasyShoot

> EasyShoot is a free screenshot app for macOS 14 and later, on the Mac App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/easyshoot-screenshot-markup/id6829547113. It captures an area, a window or the full screen, lets you annotate the image and frame it on a clean background, and never uploads anything. The interface is in English, Arabic, French, Spanish and German.

- Website: https://easyshoot.app/
- The same page in Arabic, French, Spanish and German: https://easyshoot.app/ar/, /fr/, /es/, /de/
- Sitemap: https://easyshoot.app/sitemap-index.xml
- Full text of the user guide, guides and comparisons: https://easyshoot.app/llms-full.txt
- Changelog: https://easyshoot.app/changelog/
- Support: https://easyshoot.app/support.html
- Privacy policy: https://easyshoot.app/privacy.html
- Author: Haytham A. Salama (https://haythamasalama.me)

## Features

- Capture: area, window and fullscreen, each on a global shortcut you can record yourself.
- Quick Access: a floating thumbnail after each capture to copy, save, annotate or drag into another app.
- Annotations: arrows, lines, rectangles, diamonds, ellipses, text, numbered steps, pen and pixelate. Every mark stays editable, with four corner handles to resize it. Copy, cut, paste and duplicate marks with Command-C, X, V and D.
- Style: every tool's settings live in the inspector's Style tab: Apple's six system colours with matching light fills, stroke width (thin, medium, bold or 1 to 30), solid, dashed or dotted strokes, a background (fill) for shapes and steps with an outline that can be hidden, a rounded-corners slider, a shadow slider, an angle (Shift snaps to 15°) and opacity. Arrows have a standard or swept head and bend by dragging their middle handle.
- Pixelate: pixels or blur, with a strength.
- Text looks: plain, background, soft, framed, outline, dark or custom; direction auto, left to right or right to left.
- Selection: Command-A, Shift-click or a box dragged over empty canvas selects several marks to move, restyle or delete together.
- Text: any font installed on the Mac, plus Google Fonts downloaded on demand. Arabic and Hebrew are written right-to-left with correct shaping.
- Background: a Show background switch, then a wallpaper (the Mac's own desktop pictures, or EasyShoot's Waves and Gradients), a gradient or a colour, with background blur, padding, rounded corners, shadow, shadow opacity, aspect ratio and alignment. Each slider has a Reset.
- Crop and resize: free or fixed ratios (1:1, 4:3, 16:9), resize by percent or to an exact width.
- Presets: the list starts empty, with 12 starter looks to add in Settings › Presets. Save your own style and make it the default; without a default, each screenshot starts with the last settings.
- Export: PNG, JPEG, HEIC or TIFF; copy with Shift-Command-C, save with Command-S.
- Zoom: the − and + buttons in the corner of the canvas, or Command-Plus and Command-Minus.
- Editor keys: A arrow, L line, R rectangle, O ellipse, T text, N numbered step, D diamond, P pen, B pixelate, C crop, V select.
- Look: native SwiftUI and AppKit, light and dark, Liquid Glass on macOS 26.
- Privacy: no account, no cloud, no analytics. The app only goes online to download a Google font you pick and to check the App Store for a newer version.

## Default shortcuts

- Capture area: Option-Shift-Command-4
- Capture window: Option-Shift-Command-5
- Capture fullscreen: Option-Shift-Command-3
- Annotate the clipboard image: Option-Shift-Command-7

## Install

1. Get EasyShoot from the Mac App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/easyshoot-screenshot-markup/id6829547113
2. The Welcome window takes three steps: allow Screen Recording, choose where screenshots are saved, and you're ready. EasyShoot lives in the menu bar.
3. Updates come from the App Store.

## User guide

One page per topic, in English, Arabic, French, Spanish and German: https://easyshoot.app/docs/

- [Getting started](https://easyshoot.app/docs/getting-started/): Install, allow screen capture and take your first screenshot.
- [Capture](https://easyshoot.app/docs/capture/): Area, window, full screen, or an image you already have.
- [Quick Access](https://easyshoot.app/docs/quick-access/): What happens right after a capture.
- [Mark up](https://easyshoot.app/docs/mark-up/): Arrows, shapes, numbered steps, text and pen.
- [Styles](https://easyshoot.app/docs/styles/): Fill, stroke, corners, shadow, angle and opacity.
- [Hide private details](https://easyshoot.app/docs/hide-details/): Pixelate or blur emails, names and card numbers.
- [Text](https://easyshoot.app/docs/text/): Any font, seven looks, and right-to-left text.
- [Background and crop](https://easyshoot.app/docs/background-and-crop/): Frame a shot, crop it and resize it.
- [Presets](https://easyshoot.app/docs/presets/): Start from a ready look, or save your own.
- [Export and share](https://easyshoot.app/docs/export/): Copy, save, formats and size.
- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://easyshoot.app/docs/shortcuts/): Every key in one place.
- [Settings](https://easyshoot.app/docs/settings/): General, Shortcuts, Presets, Permissions and About.
- [Privacy](https://easyshoot.app/docs/privacy/): What stays on your Mac, and when the app goes online.

## What EasyShoot does not do

- No screen recording or GIF export.
- No text recognition (OCR).
- No cloud upload or share links.
- Mac only (macOS 14 or later).
